card_summary: A company developed a system for a VFX Oscar winner, utilizing 12G-SDI for live signal transport. The system was designed to maintain signal integrity and frame-accuracy. The use of 12G-SDI in this system implies a low-latency transport method, likely paired with Genlock for synchronization. This setup would ensure accurate and reliable signal transmission, meeting the requirements for live production and post-production applications, potentially incorporating standards like ST 2110 for IP-based transport.

Technical Analysis: JPEG XS Enables 12G-SDI Replacement for Live 4K/UHD Signal Transport

At the recent NAB Show, intoPIX announced the integration of their JPEG XS codec into several broadcast equipment manufacturers' products, enabling the replacement of 12G-SDI for live 4K/UHD signal transport. This development involves the use of JPEG XS, a compression standard that allows for visually lossless compression of high-resolution video signals, making it suitable for live production applications. The technology has been adopted by several major broadcast equipment manufacturers, including those specializing in live production switchers and routers.

Operational ROI

The adoption of JPEG XS for live 4K/UHD signal transport can significantly reduce transmission costs for broadcast CTOs, as it enables the use of existing 10GbE infrastructure, rather than requiring the installation of new, high-bandwidth fiber optic cables. This can result in cost savings of up to 50% compared to traditional 12G-SDI solutions. Additionally, JPEG XS compression can reduce the latency associated with signal transport, allowing for more accurate synchronization of multiple signals in live production environments. This affects the signal routing workflow step, as it simplifies the process of transporting high-bandwidth signals over existing infrastructure.

In comparison to the existing approach of using 12G-SDI, the adoption of JPEG XS enables a more flexible and scalable signal transport solution. With 12G-SDI, each signal requires a dedicated coaxial cable, which can lead to a large number of cables and significant rack space requirements. In contrast, JPEG XS allows multiple signals to be transported over a single 10GbE link, reducing the overall hardware rack footprint and simplifying signal routing. This change operationally affects the way broadcast engineers design and implement live production systems, as they can now more easily scale their systems to meet the demands of high-bandwidth, live 4K/UHD productions.

Security & Integration

The integration of JPEG XS into live production systems must be carefully considered in terms of security and compliance with relevant broadcast standards. The use of JPEG XS compression must comply with standards such as SMPTE ST 2110-22, which defines the transport of compressed video over IP networks. Additionally, the use of JPEG XS must be integrated with other broadcast standards, such as NMOS IS-04, which provides a framework for the registration and discovery of devices on an IP network. From a cybersecurity perspective, the use of JPEG XS compression must be evaluated in terms of its potential impact on signal integrity and the overall security of the live production system.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment: The deployment of JPEG XS for live 4K/UHD signal transport requires a minimum of 10GbE network infrastructure, as well as hardware capable of supporting the JPEG XS codec, such as intoPIX's FlinQ IP cores.
  • Compatibility: The JPEG XS codec must comply with SMPTE ST 2110-22 and NMOS IS-04, ensuring seamless integration with other IP-based live production equipment.
  • What to Watch: The upcoming update to the SMPTE ST 2110 standard, which is expected to include new specifications for the transport of compressed video over IP networks, will be an important development for engineers to track, as it may impact the deployment and integration of JPEG XS in live production systems.

The adoption of JPEG XS for live 4K/UHD signal transport signals a significant shift in the way broadcast engineers approach signal transport and routing in live production environments. As a result, engineering teams should begin evaluating the use of JPEG XS in their live production systems, with a focus on ensuring compliance with relevant broadcast standards and evaluating the potential impact on signal integrity and system security.

Analysis: ST 2110 adoption enables efficient video transport for VFX workflows, supporting 4K resolution at 100 Mbps bitrate, reducing latency in post-production pipelines.
